name: Load-time layout co-design and weight permutation
scope: Examined vLLM's DeepSeek V4.1 hand-fused stack: agent_space/vllm/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/fused_layout.py, its caller nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py, the layout tests, and vLLM's composed_weight_loader. Examined Mirage MPK's weight interleaving: the shuffle_tensors/fuse_tensors graph ops, how the runtime materializes them, the Qwen3 and DeepSeek-V3 builders, the task-count helpers that set the interleave granularity, and Mirage's z3 layout resolver. Also examined PyTorch Inductor freezing (constant folding and QKV/gate-up weight concatenation) and the MegaBake code that would host such a pass: memory.py parameter bindings, plan.py CuTeLayout, the lowering of views as strided coordinate maps (lowering.py), bodies/interface.py LayoutContract, the always-rejected paired gate/up candidate in regions.py, and runtime parameter binding by reference (compiler.py). Web research covered generic compiler techniques: XLA layout assignment, JAX Layout.AUTO with device_put into the compiler-chosen format, TVM Relax LiftTransformParams, PBQP layout selection, CuTe layout algebra and its categorical foundations, Triton linear layouts over F2, Hexcute, Tilus, Graphene, equality saturation (Tensat, Glenside), and computational-invariance weight folding (SliceGPT, QuaRot). Question answered: how a generic compiler can choose activation layouts between producer and consumer bodies and fold the resulting permutations (or other invertible transforms) into weights once at load time. The aim is that no per-step shuffle, copy or extra phase remains. The item also covers what MegaBake would need for such a pass and what it would gain on the H200 MIG slice.

core_ideas.idea: Producer-side output permutation folded into weight ROWS (N dim)
core_ideas.how_it_works: A GEMM y = x W^T emits outputs in the order of W's rows. Gathering W's rows (and bias, and per-row quant scales) by perm makes the GEMM write y[:, perm], which is the consumer's preferred layout. This costs nothing per step and is bit-exact, because each output is still the same dot product. DSv4.1's q_fused_permutation sends element (h,d) to (d//16)*(H*16) + h*16 + d%16. That is a mixed-radix transpose: reshape [H,D] to [H, D/16, 16] and permute to [D/16, H, 16], which a rank-3 strided view can express. permute_on_load gathers wq_b.weight and wq_b.weight_scale with the same index (row-wise scales follow their row).

core_ideas.idea: Consumer-side input permutation folded into weight COLUMNS (K dim), with block-scale derivation
core_ideas.how_it_works: If the attention kernel writes O in a chunk-interleaved order, the next GEMM z = O W^T reads it correctly when W's columns are gathered by the same perm, since the dot product over K is permutation-invariant. o_fused_permutation interleaves 32-element chunks across the 8 heads of a wo_a group. The MXFP8 per-32 block scales are permuted by perm[::32]//32. This is legal only because the perm maps whole 32-aligned blocks to whole blocks, and a generic pass must check that. The reduction order changes, so results differ in the last ulps (the test uses 1e-3 tolerance), unlike the row case.

core_ideas.idea: Layout transparency of intermediate ops (norm, RoPE, KV insert) between the two GEMMs
core_ideas.how_it_works: The permutation reaches the attention kernel only if every op in between is layout-polymorphic or is told the layout. vLLM's fused qnorm/RoPE/KV-insert kernel takes is_q_interleaved, and a test proves bit-exactness: 'a lane owns the same 512-dim slice of its head in either layout — only the address differs'. The KV half must not inherit Q's layout. In general: elementwise ops propagate any layout, per-channel ops need their parameter permuted, and reductions over the permuted axis are invariant up to summation order. Ops that mix positions (RoPE rotate-half partners, reshapes) need the perm to commute with them or their index map rewritten.

core_ideas.idea: Load-time application through the weight-loader hook (no compiler; hand co-design)
core_ideas.how_it_works: composed_weight_loader wraps the parameter's loader: it runs the original copy, then param.data.copy_(fn(param)). There is no separate graph pass; the module that owns the kernel also owns the weight transform. The transform is not idempotent: running it twice (multi-shard params, weight reload) double-permutes, and vLLM's reload accounting already had to special-case the double copy. Kernel availability is gated on topology (heads per wo_a group == 8, TP), because the permutation constants are tied to the kernel.

core_ideas.idea: Horizontal fusion through weight interleaving whose granularity is set by the task decomposition (Mirage MPK)
core_ideas.how_it_works: Mirage concatenates or interleaves sibling weights into one GEMM. For QKV, shuffle_tensors(num_groups=num_kv_heads) lays out [Q_g, K_g, V_g] per KV group, so each attention task's inputs are contiguous. For gate/up, num_groups = linear task count / 2, so each linear task's output tile holds matching gate and up halves and silu_mul task i reads exactly one producer tile. In the DSV3 demo a plain torch.cat gives wrong results: the interleave must follow grid_for_rmsnorm_linear_layer, and the FP8 block scales are interleaved the same way. The runtime materializes ShuffledTorchTensor once at init with cudaMemcpy2DAsync into a new cudaMalloc buffer, keeping the originals, so those weights take 2x memory. fuse_tensors (plain concat) is virtual: the sub-tensors keep their own pointers.

core_ideas.idea: Constraint/optimization-based layout assignment over the whole graph
core_ideas.how_it_works: Mirage's transpiler assigns innermost dimensions and swizzles for all device and shared tensors with z3::optimize. Hand-set costs (no wide copy 4000, no ldmatrix 10000, no cp.async 20000, swizzle 1000) are summed and minimized under producer/consumer equality constraints. Graph inputs, including weights, are pinned to their given strides, so Mirage never rewrites weights through this path. XLA LayoutAssignment propagates constraints from layout-constrained ops through the graph and inserts copies where they conflict. JAX lets the entry parameters be AUTO: compile, read compiled.input_formats, and device_put the weights into that layout once. Anderson & Gregg pose primitive-plus-layout selection, with conversion costs on edges, as PBQP and solve it optimally.

core_ideas.idea: Lifting weight-only subgraphs into a load-time function (constant folding without freezing the model)
core_ideas.how_it_works: TVM Relax LiftTransformParams splits every computation that depends only on parameters (transposes, layout_transform, concat, quant repack) into a separate transform_params function. That function runs once at load and its outputs replace the parameters; the InplaceTransformParams RFC addresses the 2x memory. Inductor freezing inlines parameters as constants, runs constant_fold and binary folding, and pattern-matches 2–3 mm/addmm with a shared input into one GEMM on torch.cat of the weights (check_concat_weights requires get_attr weights). After that, weights can no longer be updated unless the graph is re-frozen.

core_ideas.idea: Layout algebras as the IR for which permutations are expressible and how to derive them
core_ideas.how_it_works: In CuTe, a layout is a hierarchical shape:stride function. With composition, complement, logical_divide and right_inverse, the producer-to-consumer conversion is consumer^-1 ∘ producer, so the needed permutation can be computed rather than hard-coded. Both DSv4.1 permutations are single CuTe layouts, for example Q = ((16, D/16), H):((1, 16H), 16). Triton linear layouts model layouts as F2 matrices over index bits, which also covers swizzles and register/lane/warp distributions; layout conversion becomes a matrix product, and RemoveLayoutConversions propagates layouts to cancel conversions. Hexcute infers thread-value layouts and task mappings by type inference over constraints. Tilus uses an algebraic register-tile layout so low-precision tiles can be reinterpreted without conversion, which is what weight pre-swizzling for mixed precision relies on. Graphene makes shape/stride layouts and tile decompositions first-class IR. All of these are kernel-internal; none rewrites model weights by itself.

Represent each value's possible layouts as e-class members. Rewrite rules state the algebraic facts: transpose(transpose(x)) = x; matmul(x, W)[perm] = matmul(x, W[perm,:]); matmul(x[:,perm], W) = matmul(x, W[:,perm]); elementwise(x[perm]) = elementwise(x)[perm]; concat(mm(x, A), mm(x, B)) = mm(x, concat(A, B)). Saturate, then extract the cheapest program with a cost model that charges zero for transforms applied to parameter-only subterms, since they are lifted to load time. Tensat does this for graph substitutions and Glenside for access-pattern (layout) rewriting. This finds global solutions such as permuting the entire residual stream. Extraction is costly (ILP), and an e-graph can blow up on 30+ layer graphs unless rules are restricted to per-layer templates.

core_ideas.idea: Generalization beyond permutations: computational invariance (fold any invertible transform into weights)
core_ideas.how_it_works: A permutation is a special orthogonal matrix. SliceGPT and QuaRot fold orthogonal Q into adjacent weights (W_out Q, Q^T W_in) across RMSNorm, after first folding the norm gamma into the next linear's columns. The same machinery folds RMSNorm gamma: (x·rstd·g) W^T = rstd·(x (W·diag(g))^T). The norm then becomes a per-row scalar applied in the GEMM epilogue, and the sum of squares can be computed by the GEMM CTA itself. LayerNorm also folds, using precomputed column sums of W for the mean term. These are not bit-exact, because rounding changes when bf16 W·g is formed. llama.cpp's converter permutes q/k rows to switch RoPE between rotate-half and interleaved pairing; this is legal because q·k is invariant under the same head-dim permutation of q and k.

core_ideas.idea: Accumulator-fragment-derived permutation for in-register epilogue fusion (e.g. RoPE in the QKV GEMM epilogue)
core_ideas.how_it_works: An epilogue that needs element pairs (RoPE partners, gate/up pairs, block-quant groups) avoids shuffles when the pair lands in one thread's registers. The MMA atom's C TV-layout (WGMMA m64nNk16 on SM90; TMEM 32dp32b loads on SM100) says which (row, col) a thread holds. Composing its inverse with the pairing relation gives the row permutation to fold into W. With swapAB the feature dimension is WGMMA's M, so features r and r+8 are held by one thread, not features 2c and 2c+1. The right permutation therefore differs between swapAB and non-swapAB tiles and between SM90 and SM100. This is a hardware-derived constant and must be computed from the atom, not hard-coded.

megabake_status.idea: Producer-side output permutation folded into weight ROWS
megabake_status.evidence: src/megabake/compiler.py:876-901 binds parameters by reference to the user's live tensors; no derived or transformed parameter storage exists in CompiledKernel or memory.py:625-681.
megabake_status.notes: The IR can already express the target layouts: views lower to strided coordinate maps (lowering.py:720-760), and bodies declare input layouts via LayoutContract (bodies/interface.py:95-108). What is missing is a pass that changes a parameter's physical layout, plus the storage and invalidation to own the result.

megabake_status.idea: Consumer-side input permutation folded into weight COLUMNS
megabake_status.evidence: Same as above; the GEMM body accepts only K-major or M-major operands (bodies/gemm.py:1367-1406). A permuted K would have to be a TMA-describable strided layout or be folded into the weight.
megabake_status.notes: Changes the reduction order, so it conflicts with teacher-forced bit-exact verification. MegaBake would need a tolerance-based numerical policy flag for K-permutations.

megabake_status.evidence: Generic elementwise and reduction bodies index through explicit strides (lowering.py _view_program; IndexedLoad strides). The attention body reads strided loads (bodies/attention.py:287-301).
megabake_status.notes: Layout polymorphism already exists implicitly, because every load is a strided index map. There is no analysis that proves a permutation commutes with an op (per-channel params, rotate-half partners), and no per-channel parameter co-permutation.

megabake_status.idea: Load-time application through a loader hook
megabake_status.evidence: MegaBake compiles a captured HF module, not a loader. Weights already exist when compile() runs.
megabake_status.notes: The equivalent is a transform at compile time on the bound parameters (a LiftTransformParams-style prologue) plus a cheap per-call staleness check (tensor._version or data_ptr). A cache key with a transform revision would extend cache.py:95.

megabake_status.idea: Horizontal fusion via weight interleaving keyed to task decomposition
megabake_status.evidence: regions.py:2159-2290 detects gate/up/SiLU/mul as a gated_mlp candidate but always rejects it (L2240 'paired GEMM provider is not implemented'; PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:282). No QKV horizontal fusion; PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:79 says K and V fill 3 of 60 CTAs. ARCHITECTURE.md:318 already says 'do not concatenate weights every call'.
megabake_status.notes: The candidate's cost model charges packing_cost_bytes per call (regions.py:2247). That is wrong once packing is done at load. The interleave period must come from the selected GEMM tile (16/32/64 swapAB row tiles), not from a model constant.

megabake_status.evidence: Layouts are taken from the consumer tile map or the value strides in _make_boundary_binding (memory.py:779-823). There is no search over layouts; the body search (ARCHITECTURE.md:397-403) treats layout as fixed input.
megabake_status.notes: MegaBake already searches body configurations, so layout could be another dimension of the same search, as a per-edge PBQP cost table.

megabake_status.idea: Lifting weight-only subgraphs to load time
megabake_status.evidence: lowering.py:2442-2452 lowers get_attr as attribute constants, but parameter-only computations (e.g. a cat or transpose of weights in the FX graph) are lowered as per-call phases (_concat_program, _copy_program).
megabake_status.notes: A pre-pass that partitions parameter-only FX nodes into a 'transform_params' graph, run once with PyTorch, is cheap to implement on the post-grad FX graph.

megabake_status.evidence: plan.py:41-71 CuTeLayout is flat shape/stride plus an optional XOR swizzle. CuTe DSL is the backend, so full CuTe algebra is available at codegen.
megabake_status.notes: Mixed-radix permutations need rank expansion (e.g. [H*D] to [H, D/16, 16]). Nested layouts and composition/inverse are not used at the planning level.

megabake_status.evidence: No e-graph infrastructure; region formation is pattern matching (regions.py).
megabake_status.notes: Probably overkill as a first step. Per-layer local rules plus a PBQP solve give most of the benefit.

megabake_status.evidence: RMSNorm is matched and run as its own region (PERFORMANCE_REPORT.md:54). ROADMAP.md:113 lists 49 RMSNorms at about 5 us each on 1.7B (before folding).
megabake_status.notes: Not bit-exact. Needs an opt-in numerical policy.

megabake_status.evidence: The GEMM epilogue supports only a bias add (bodies/gemm.py:1923-1940); RoPE runs as generated elementwise bodies.
megabake_status.notes: Depends first on multi-op epilogues; the permutation then removes the cross-thread shuffle.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Tile-aligned layouts that make producer→consumer dependencies 1:1 per tile, enabling per-tile event counters instead of grid barriers
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: In a multi-kernel graph the consumer kernel waits for the whole producer grid, through stream order or PDL griddepcontrol.wait, whatever the layout. Choosing the layout so that consumer task i reads exactly producer tile i (Mirage: QKV interleaved per KV head, gate/up per task) only pays off when the runtime can signal and wait per tile, which a persistent megakernel with event counters can (ROADMAP step 10).
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multikernel_substitute: PDL overlaps the consumer prologue with the producer tail, but the data dependency still waits for the whole grid. Stream-K or fused kernels for fixed pairs (vLLM's fused attention kernel) cover only hand-chosen pairs.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Same-CTA producer→consumer chaining with data in SMEM/registers
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: Shared memory and registers do not survive a kernel boundary. If the layout pass makes the producer's output tile match the consumer's input tile (same interleave, same fragment order), a persistent CTA can run consumer work on its own tile without a global round trip. Examples: gate/up into SiLU into the down-projection K-slice, or the QKV tile of KV group g into that group's attention.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multikernel_substitute: Manually fused kernels for specific op pairs (a FlashInfer/vLLM fused MLP); L2 residency between kernels is not guaranteed.

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: One weight layout chosen jointly for the whole program's schedule, including the work-assignment order
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: A megakernel compiler sees every consumer of every weight and the global task order. It can therefore pick, for example, a weight layout that makes cross-phase L2 prefetch (ROADMAP step 9) stream contiguously in the order CTAs will consume tiles. Separate kernels are compiled in isolation and cannot coordinate weight stream order across launches.
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.nearest_multikernel_substitute: Per-kernel prepacking (Marlin repack, vLLM process_weights_after_loading) gives the best layout per kernel, but nothing coordinates the stream order across kernels. [uncertain: the prefetch-ordering benefit is not measured]

megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.opportunity: Note: the basic load-time permutation is NOT megakernel-exclusive
megakernel_exclusive_opportunities.why_multikernel_cannot: vLLM's DSv4.1 stack is a multi-kernel graph (CUDA graphs) and gets the full benefit of permute_on_load. Inductor freezing does QKV concat in multi-kernel graphs too. The exclusive part is only the tile-granular sync and locality that the layout enables.

measured_or_reported_gains: vLLM DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega-attention (permuted wq_b/wo_a + fused RoPE/inverse-RoPE/FP8 cast), GB300, CUDA graphs on, 64-head model: TP1 29/29 us at s_q=1 up to 96 vs 140 us at s_q=512 (up to 1.45x), TP2–TP8 within a few percent, with a fixed ~2 us penalty at small s_q. The gain is not attributable to the permutation alone; the permutation is what makes the fusion free of per-step shuffles (flash_mla_mega_attn.py:64-86).

Mirage MPK reports 1.2–6.7x end-to-end latency reduction over kernel-per-op systems for its whole megakernel. QKV/gate-up interleaving is one enabling ingredient and is not separately ablated [uncertain].
Hexcute: 1.7–11.28x over existing DL compilers on mixed-type operators, up to 2.91x end-to-end (v1 abstract) [uncertain for v3].
Tilus: 1.75x over Triton, 2.61x over Ladder, 1.29x over QuantLLM, 1.03x over Marlin on low-precision GEMM (arXiv v3 abstract).
Linear Layouts (Triton): reduces backend engineering effort and fixes layout bugs; per-kernel speedups are reported in the paper but not checked here [uncertain].
Anderson & Gregg PBQP layout+primitive selection: significant speedups on desktop and embedded CPUs vs per-layer greedy (no single number verified) [uncertain].
MegaBake baseline for context: decode kernel 135M 1.50 ms vs Inductor 1.38 ms; 1.7B 2.97 vs 2.42 ms; Qwen2-0.5B 1.58 vs 1.64 ms (artifacts/full_model_2026-10-18).

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Fold RMSNorm gamma into the following GEMM weights and apply rstd as a per-row epilogue scale. The sum of squares is computed inside the GEMM CTAs, since decode activations are 576–2048 elements per token.
expected_impact_on_megabake.decode_estimate: 1.7B: about 49 norms. ROADMAP lists them at ~5 us each (0.245 ms) before interval folding; folding has since cut that. If each norm's residual cost is 1.5–3 us (recompute rounds plus the activation write and read), removing them saves ~0.07–0.15 ms of 2.97 ms (2–5%). On 135M (61 norms, 0.21 ms in the older breakdown) the share is larger, about 5–10% [uncertain].
expected_impact_on_megabake.prefill_estimate: Small. Prefill is dominated by GEMM inefficiency above 64 tokens.
expected_impact_on_megabake.caveat: Not bit-exact; needs an opt-in numerics policy. Gemma's (1+w) and LayerNorm (column-sum term) both fold.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Paired gate/up GEMM with load-time interleave at the selected tile's row period and SiLU·mul in the epilogue (unblocks regions.py:2240).
expected_impact_on_megabake.decode_estimate: Removes the gate/up intermediate write and read (negligible bytes at decode) and the SiLU·mul phase or its recompute. That is about 0.5–1 barrier interval per layer: 0.35–0.7 us × 24–30 layers ≈ 10–20 us. It also halves GEMM phase pipeline start-up for the pair (~1–2 us per layer) ⇒ ~30–60 us total, 1–3% [uncertain].
expected_impact_on_megabake.prefill_estimate: Saves the 2×M×I intermediate round trip: at 256 tokens on 1.7B, 2×256×8192×2 B ≈ 8 MB per layer ≈ 4 us at 2.2 TB/s, ≈ 0.1 ms total.
expected_impact_on_megabake.caveat: The interleave period must divide the tile height of every bucket's selected config, or one packed copy per period is needed.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: QKV horizontal fusion (concat or interleave by KV group).
expected_impact_on_megabake.decode_estimate: 135M: Q has 9 swapAB 64-row tiles and K/V 3 each; they already share a barrier interval via _level_order (schedule.py:1304-1330). The gain is mainly one pipeline start-up instead of three and a better tile mix: ~1 us/layer × 30 ≈ 30 us (~2% of 1.50 ms). 1.7B (MHA, 32 tiles each) gains less, ~10 us. Interleaving by KV group is the prerequisite for per-group events once ROADMAP step 10 lands: an attention head group could then start as soon as its QKV tile is done, saving up to one barrier (~0.7 us) per layer.
expected_impact_on_megabake.prefill_estimate: Larger N per GEMM gives better wave quantization on 60 SMs; a few percent of GEMM time [uncertain].
expected_impact_on_megabake.caveat: Qwen2 bias must be concatenated or interleaved too; the bias epilogue already exists.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: Accumulator-derived row permutation of q/k weights so RoPE runs in the QKV GEMM epilogue.
expected_impact_on_megabake.decode_estimate: Removes the RoPE elementwise work or recompute: ~0.5–1 us/layer ⇒ 12–30 us [uncertain]. Requires multi-op epilogues first.
expected_impact_on_megabake.prefill_estimate: Saves one read and write of Q/K: small.
expected_impact_on_megabake.caveat: The KV cache then stores permuted K. That is fine internally, but external cache consumers or prefix sharing with another engine would see a permuted layout.

expected_impact_on_megabake.change: DSv4.1-style chunk-interleaved Q/O layouts for a tensor-core attention body.
expected_impact_on_megabake.decode_estimate: ~0 today. MegaBake's attention body is SIMT, one query row at a time (bodies/attention.py:275-280), so no consumer demands an exotic layout. This becomes relevant only with a tensor-core decode or prefill attention body.
expected_impact_on_megabake.prefill_estimate: Relevant only after a FlashAttention-style prefill body exists.

expected_impact_on_megabake.note: Overall: a generic layout-and-weight-rewrite pass is worth roughly 3–10% of decode kernel time on the tested models [uncertain]. That is smaller than events in the table launch (step 10) or L2 weight prefetch (step 9). Its bigger value is as an enabler: tile-granular events, paired epilogues, and same-CTA chaining all need the producer's output tiling to match the consumer's input tiling.

generality_and_overfitting_risk.assessment: Kernel-specific and model-specific: HEAD_DIM=512, Q_CHUNK=16, O_CHUNK=32, WV_GROUP_SIZE=8 (fused_layout.py:17-20). Availability is gated on heads per wo_a group == 8 and TP (flash_mla_mega_attn.py:138-162). The permutation is hand-derived from one kernel's register layout. Not a technique to copy literally; copy the invariance and the test pattern (permute the weight, compare against permuting the activation).

Overfit. grid_for_rmsnorm_linear_layer returns 96 or 64, with the comment 'enough to cover all Qwen3 model? Please update ... if you meet any incompatibility' and a size//256 workaround for a numerics bug (python/mirage/mpk/models/utils.py:3-16). Because the gate/up interleave and the silu_mul grid both derive from it, the weight layout is tied to a Qwen3-tuned task count. The z3 layout costs (4000/10000/20000/1000) are hand-set (resolve_tensor_layout.cc:50-76). Per-model builders (demo_hopper.py) choose num_groups by hand.

Matches the HF silu(gate)*up shape specifically (regions.py:2159-2230). GELU-gated (Gemma) and SwiGLU variants with a different operand order need a generic 'two contractions sharing input feeding a binary op' matcher. packing_cost_bytes (regions.py:2247) assumes per-call packing; a load-time pass should cost it as zero per call plus a one-time memory cost.

SWAP_AB_MAX_ROWS=64 and SWAP_AB_ROW_TILES=(16,32,64) (bodies/gemm.py:1893-1896) are fixed for SM90 WGMMA. Any interleave period derived from them must be read from the selected body config, never hard-coded. Fold limits (schedule.py:1383-1386: 2/6/6 rounds/phases) are tuned on the decode traces of the tested models.

(1) Derive permutations from layout algebra: needed_perm = consumer_layout^-1 ∘ producer_layout, with consumer layouts taken from the MMA atom's TV-layout and selected tile. (2) Legality from algebraic invariance rules (N-perm is free and exact; K-perm is free but changes reduction order; elementwise ops are transparent; per-channel params co-permute; block-scale perms must map whole blocks). These are model-agnostic facts, not pattern matches. (3) Choose among candidate layouts by measured or cost-model search per edge (PBQP or ILP, as Anderson & Gregg do), not fixed costs. (4) Handle tied weights (lm_head/embedding) and multi-consumer parameters as constraints: one physical copy per distinct required layout. (5) Verify every rewrite with the vLLM-style equivalence test, generated automatically per rewrite.

hardware_portability: Row/column weight permutation, concat/interleave, and norm-gamma folding are hardware-agnostic math. They carry to SM80, SM90, SM100, AMD and TPU unchanged.

Which permutation is wanted is hardware-specific: WGMMA (SM90) accumulator fragments, TMEM load shapes (SM100 tcgen05, 32dp32b/16dp256b), mma.sync m16n8k16 (SM80), and swapAB vs normal orientation each give a different pairing of rows/columns per thread. Derive it from the CuTe MMA atom and copy atom of the chosen body. Then retargeting changes only the atom, and the pass recomputes the weight permutation. Triton linear layouts and CuTe both support this derivation.

TMA (SM90/SM100) can load and store rank-≤5 boxes. A mixed-radix permutation such as DSv4.1's Q layout can be a TMA descriptor over a rank-3 view instead of a weight rewrite. On SM80 (cp.async) such a permutation costs address arithmetic, so folding into weights matters more there.

Block-scaled formats (MXFP8/NVFP4 on SM100, FP8 128x128 blocks on SM90 DeepSeek-style) restrict legal permutations to block-aligned ones. The legality check must be parameterized by the format's block shape.
Weight pre-swizzling for SMEM bank layouts (Tilus, Marlin) is per-architecture and per-tile. Keep it out of the persisted weight cache key unless the target is part of the key.

recommended_actions.action: Add a 'transform_params' stage: partition parameter-only FX subgraphs (transpose, cat, view, dtype casts of weights) out of the captured graph and run them once at compile/bind time with PyTorch. Store the results in CompiledKernel as owned buffers and bind them instead of the user's tensors. Check staleness per call cheaply (parameter tensor._version plus data_ptr) and recompute or invalidate on change.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Removes any per-call weight copies or concats and is the substrate for every other action. Enables Inductor-freezing-style QKV concat without freezing the module.
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/compiler.py (_current_parameter_tensors, CompiledKernel), src/megabake/frontend.py (parameter_names), src/megabake/memory.py (_boundary_bindings: kind 'derived_parameter'), src/megabake/cache.py (transform revision in key)

recommended_actions.action: Implement the paired gate/up GEMM provider. Interleave gate and up rows at period P = the selected swapAB row tile (or a divisor of every bucket's tile), and run SiLU or GELU · mul in the epilogue. Fix packing_cost_bytes to be a one-time cost. Generalize the matcher to 'two contractions with a shared input feeding a binary pointwise op'.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: ~30–60 us decode on 135M/1.7B (1–3%), ~0.1 ms prefill at 256 tokens on 1.7B [uncertain]. Removes one phase per layer.

recommended_actions.action: Horizontal GEMM fusion for N contractions sharing an input (QKV, and MoE shared/routed gate-up). Interleave by the consumer's natural group (KV head group for attention), with bias co-permuted.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: ~10–30 us decode (1–2%). Prerequisite for per-group events in step 10.
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/regions.py (new candidate), src/megabake/lowering.py (concat of parameters routed to transform_params), src/megabake/bodies/attention.py (accept grouped layout via strides)

recommended_actions.action: Promote CuTeLayout in plan.py to nested (hierarchical) shape:stride with composition and right_inverse helpers, or map directly onto cute.make_layout at planning time. Add a check that a permutation is a mixed-radix transpose and therefore view-expressible.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Enables computing permutations from body contracts instead of hard-coding them. No direct speedup.

recommended_actions.action: Layout-assignment pass. For each producer→(transparent chain)→consumer edge, enumerate the consumer's preferred layouts from its LayoutContract. Fold the permutation into producer weight rows (exact) or consumer weight columns (numerics flag), co-permuting per-channel params, biases and block scales. Solve per layer as a small PBQP over edges, with costs from the existing body-measurement search.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Enabler for epilogue RoPE and future tensor-core attention layouts; 0–30 us now.

recommended_actions.action: Opt-in numerics policy 'fold_norm_weights': fold RMSNorm/LayerNorm gamma (and the Gemma 1+w form) into the following linear's columns, and turn the norm into an rstd row-scale computed in the GEMM CTA and applied in the epilogue.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: 2–5% decode on 1.7B, 5–10% on 135M [uncertain]. Largest of the weight-rewrite gains.
recommended_actions.files_to_touch: src/megabake/regions.py (norm region), src/megabake/bodies/gemm.py (row-scale epilogue + prologue reduction), verification tolerance in tools/diff_intermediates.py

recommended_actions.action: Auto-generate equivalence tests for every weight rewrite, following test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py: run the original op on a permuted activation vs the rewritten op. Use rtol=0 for N-permutations, and a declared tolerance for K-permutations and folded norms.
recommended_actions.expected_gain: Correctness safety net, which keeps generality honest.
